name: BTS5030-1EJA
title: Single-channel 30 mΩ smart high-side power switch, PROFET+ 12V
summary: The BTS5030-1EJA is a one-channel high-side switch for 12 V automotive loads: an N-channel vertical power DMOS driven by an on-chip charge pump, with 30 mΩ typical on-resistance at 25 °C, in an 8-lead DSO package whose exposed pad is the supply. It is aimed at lamps up to two P21W bulbs, LEDs, and resistive, inductive or capacitive loads with high inrush. Protection covers voltage-dependent current limiting, absolute and dynamic over-temperature shutdown with automatic restart, an inductive-load clamp, and loss of ground; the IS pin returns a current proportional to the load (kILIS about 2180) or a fixed fault current, enabled by DEN.
key_figures: 30 mΩ typ at 25 °C; 60 mΩ max at TJ = 150 °C

circuits.title: Application diagram
circuits.description: A microcontroller drives one lamp through the switch. Its two outputs reach IN and DEN through 4.7 kΩ resistors, and the IS current is turned into a voltage on RIS (1.2 kΩ), then passed through RSENSE and RA/D (4.7 kΩ each) to an A/D input, filtered by CSENSE and clamped by the 7 V Zener Z1. The battery comes in through the wiring to VS, with CVS (100 nF) and the 36 V Zener Z2 to ground. The device ground returns through RGND (1 kΩ) in parallel with the BAS21 diode D. On the output, RPD (47 kΩ) and COUT0 (4.7 nF) go to ground, and the PNP T1 can switch the battery onto ROL (1.5 kΩ) to pull the output up for open-load-in-OFF diagnosis. The lamp hangs on the output wiring.

notes: The microcontroller ground (Vss, CSENSE, Z1, RIS) is a separate net from the module ground that takes CVS, Z2, RGND, D, RPD, COUT0 and the lamp.
Pins 6, 7 and 8 form the one OUT node; the exposed pad is VS.

operation.text: The switch is an N-channel vertical DMOS whose gate is driven above the supply by an internal charge pump. Its on-resistance rises with junction temperature and climbs steeply when VS falls toward about 4.5 V. A high level on IN turns the DMOS on with a controlled slope chosen for low electromagnetic emission.

With a resistive load, tON_DELAY runs from the IN edge to VOUT reaching 10 % of VS and tON to 90 % of VS; tOFF_DELAY runs from the falling IN edge to VOUT dropping to 90 % of VS and tOFF to 10 %. The slew rates are measured between 30 % and 70 % of VS.

When an inductive load is turned off, the inductance pulls OUT below ground. A clamp, ZDS(AZ), between drain and source holds OUT at VS − VDS(AZ) so the DMOS does not avalanche, and the stored energy is spent in the switch. The load inductance is therefore limited by the allowed single-pulse energy EAS.

A voltage on OUT above VS drives an inverse current IL(INV) from OUT to VS through the body diode of the DMOS. IN still controls the output, with one exception: a turn-on command that arrives during inverse current waits until the inverse current has stopped. Diagnosis during inverse current reports open load in OFF for an off channel and open load in ON for an on channel, with the over-temperature signal suppressed. A false diagnosis may appear briefly when the inverse voltage first appears; otherwise, and once it is gone, the diagnosis matches the output. None of the protection functions operate during inverse current.

If the module ground is lost while the load stays grounded, the device turns off, or stays off, whatever IN does. Series resistors between the microcontroller and IN and DEN are recommended so the channel goes off if the device ground is lost. A small current IOUT(GND) can still flow from OUT. ZGND, the ground network, can be a resistor or a diode.

VS(OP) is the lowest supply at which the switch can be turned on and off; VS(UV) is the lowest supply at which it can stay on. With VS under VS(UV) the switch is off. Once VS is above VS(OP) it can be turned on, and the protection works while it is on, but the diagnosis is only guaranteed with VS inside the VNOM range.

The logic is protected by a Zener clamp ZD(AZ) whose current is limited by a ground resistor. With VS above VS(AZ), the power transistor conducts and the voltage across the logic is clamped; the internal ground then sits at VS − VS(AZ), and IN and DEN rise with it through their ESD Zeners to a level set by the driving circuit. An on channel remains on through the overvoltage; an off channel can be turned on. For VS between VBAT(SC) and VDS(AZ) the output transistor still follows IN, but an on channel is outside its specifications and loses lifetime, short-circuit robustness and EAS capability in particular. A 150 Ω ground resistor gives better results than a diode with 1 kΩ.

With the battery reversed, the DMOS body diode conducts and dissipates power, its current set by the load. The currents into GND and the logic pins must be kept within the absolute maximum ratings by external resistors: RGND limits the Zener current, RIN and RDEN limit the logic and ESD-stage current, and RSENSE limits what flows in the sense transistor, which then conducts like a diode. RDEN = RIN = RSENSE = 4.7 kΩ is recommended. ZGND can be a 150 Ω resistor, or a Schottky diode with 1 kΩ in parallel; where overvoltage need not be survived the Schottky-plus-1 kΩ form can replace RGND, with an optional parallel capacitor for EMC. No protection works under reverse polarity.

On overload, such as a cold lamp filament's inrush or a short to ground, the current is first held at IL(SC) to keep the power in the switch safe. The limit depends on VDS: about 47 A up to VDS = 15 V, falling linearly to about 23 A at VDS = 20 V and staying there up to 28 V. The DMOS heats during limiting, which also changes the current.

The channel has an absolute temperature sensor (TJ(SC)) and a dynamic one that trips on a temperature rise ΔTJ(SW) across the die. Either turns the channel off and holds it off until it has cooled; it then turns on again by itself if IN is still high. ΔTSTEP is the heating caused by the overcurrent. The sense output shows IIS(FAULT) during overload with DEN high, and stays at IIS(FAULT) rather than toggling with the restarts.

With DEN high, IS gives a current proportional to load current, IIS = IL / kILIS, unless a hard fault is present (short to ground, current limiting, over-temperature, excess dynamic temperature rise, or open load in OFF), in which case it gives IIS(FAULT). With DEN low IS is high impedance. Sense accuracy varies with load current and temperature. IS has its own clamp, ZIS(AZ), rated by VIS(AZ).
A pull-down resistor RIS on IS turns the sense current into a voltage. It must be above 560 Ω to limit dissipation in the sense circuit; 1.2 kΩ is typical.

Where better accuracy is wanted near half the nominal current, the ratio can be calibrated at one point (IL3, TJ = +25 °C). After that single calibration the drift of kILIS over temperature and voltage is bounded by ΔkILIS, so further calibration points are not needed.

tsIS(ON) runs from IN and DEN rising together to the sense current settling; tsIS(ON_DEN) applies when the load current is already steady and only DEN rises; tsIS(LC) covers a step in load current; tsIS(OFF) runs from DEN falling to IIS dropping below half its value.

With the channel on, a leakage path such as humidity can still carry some current through an open load. IL(OL) is the threshold: below it, with DEN selected, the device flags a failure and the sense current is under IIS(OL); above it the sense current is at least IIS(OL).

Open-load detection with the channel off uses an external pull-up ROL from the output to the battery, sized against the total leakage (IL(OFF) plus external leakage) and the threshold VOL(OFF). A switch SOL in series with ROL is recommended to save standby current. With the load missing, the output rises to nearly VS; the device takes an output above VOL(OFF) as open load and the sense output goes to IIS(FAULT). An optional RPD can pull the output to 0 V so it does not float, and also serves short-to-battery detection. Between IN falling and DEN rising for this check, tsIS(OT_BLANK) must elapse, or VOUT is not settled and the result may be false.

A short from OUT to VS carries part or all of the load current, so less flows in the DMOS and the sense current drops. With the channel off, the open-load-in-OFF comparator also detects the short when an external resistor RSC_VS from OUT to ground is fitted.

IN and DEN accept 3.3 V and 5 V logic and suit PWM. Each is a voltage-threshold comparator with hysteresis (a Schmitt trigger), so the output is only ever on or off and slow edges cause no undefined state. The switching point lies somewhere in the band from the VIN(L) maximum to the VIN(H) minimum and varies with process and temperature. An unused input is left open, or tied through a resistor to the device ground, not the module ground. DEN has the same input structure as IN.

RthJA is simulated on a 2s2p board: 1.5 mm FR4, outer copper 70 µm, inner copper 35 µm, and nine vias beneath the exposed pad. The 1s0p curves use a single-layer board with a footprint-only, 300 mm² or 600 mm² copper area under the tab.
Characterisation used 3 lots of 3 devices each, at VS = 8 V, 13.5 V and 18 V over temperature. A characteristic with no supply dependence is shown at 13.5 V only.
The protection functions keep the IC from destruction in fault conditions outside the normal operating range; they are not designed for continuous or repetitive operation.

PG-DSO-8-43 EP follows JEDEC MS-012 variation BA. Body length and width exclude plastic or metal protrusion of up to 0.15 mm per side [1]; dambar protrusion adds at most 0.1 mm in total to the lead width [2]. The package is green: RoHS compliant with a lead-free finish, suitable for lead-free soldering to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020.
